structured_output.summary: Two concrete correctness issues found relating to transaction ordering and delayed coordinator replies; the rest of the recovery/ticket-consumption logic appears sound.
findings: invocation.rs request_attached_ticket: the idempotent already-requested fast path is ordered incorrectly. The function first queries attached_local_plans/leases for released=0 AND release_pending=0 AND state='granted' to derive key_json, and only afterward checks attached_local_invocations for a prior record to short-circuit and return the existing operation id. If cleanup/release begins concurrently for this attempt (setting release_pending=1, or the lease advancing) while a Ticket request is still outstanding awaiting a coordinator reply, a legitimate retry call to request_attached_ticket for that same already-requested invocation will fail on the key_json query_row (no matching row) instead of returning the previously stored operation id. The prior-record lookup should happen before, or independent of, re-deriving the plan's current live/unreleased status, since a pending request must remain retryable regardless of the plan's state changing underneath it.

cleanup.rs apply() is only invoked from record_attached_cleanup. Its first block links a cleanup seal to an existing attached_tickets row (cleanup_json IS NULL), and its second block only recovers cleanups for tickets provably missing via attached_grants/inventory-recovery correlation. Under a delayed-coordinator-reply ordering where the executor cleanup seal is recorded locally before the AuthorizeInvocation reply has persisted the Ticket row (ticket not yet in attached_tickets, and not yet resolvable via the grants/inventory path either), neither branch of apply() links the seal to the eventual ticket, and nothing shown re-invokes cleanup::apply when the ticket is later written. Unless the ticket-consumption path (not shown, presumably in manager::consume_ticket) also calls cleanup::apply, a cleanup seal recorded ahead of its Ticket could be stranded in attached_local_cleanup without ever populating cleanup_json on the ticket. Worth confirming against that call site.
